{{nihongo|'''Shimotate Matsubara Shrine'''|下立松原神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Awa Province (Chiba)]].

There are two shrines of the same name, one in former {{ill|Shirahama, Wakayama|Q1202728|qid=Q1202728}} and one in former {{ill|Chikura, Chiba|Q5097510|qid=Q5097510}}. Both enshrine {{ill|Otori-sama|Q10939697|qid=Q10939697|lt=Ame-no-Hiwashi-no-Mikoto}} as principal deity and claim succession to the {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}} "Shimotate Matsubara Shrine" of {{ill|Awa Province (Chiba)|ceb|Awa (baranggay)|ckb|پارێزگای ئاوا (چیبا)|cs|Provincie Awa (Čiba)|de|Provinz Awa (Chiba)|es|Provincia de Awa (Chiba)|fa|ولایت آوا (چیبا)|fr|Province d'Awa (Chiba)|gl|Provincia de Awa, Chiba|hak|Awa-koet (Tōkaidō)|id|Provinsi Awa (Chiba)|it|Awa (provincia, Chiba)|ja|安房国|ko|아와국 (도카이도)|lt|Avos žemė (Čiba)|nl|Awa (provincie in Chiba)|pt|Província de Awa (Chiba)|ru|Ава (Канто)|simple|Awa Province (Chiba)|sk|Awa (provincia, Čiba)|sr|Провинција Ава (Хоншу)|tr|Awa (vilayet, Chiba)|uk|Провінція Ава (Канто)|zh|安房國|zh_min_nan|Awa-kok (Tôkaidô)|zh_yue|安房國|qid=Q1053044}}{{ill|Asai District, Chiba|ja|朝夷郡|simple|Asai District, Chiba|qid=Q4803406}}. This was long disputed, but no decisive evidence emerged and both claims remain.

Both shrine traditions say it began when Yubutsu-nushi-no-Mikoto, grandson of Ame-no-Hiwashi-no-Mikoto who came to Awa with {{ill|Amatomi no Mikoto|Q24899653|qid=Q24899653}}, enshrined Ame-no-Hiwashi-no-Mikoto in the first year of {{ill|Emperor Jimmu|Q200188|qid=Q200188}}.

The Shirahama shrine in Minamibōsō enshrines Ame-no-Hiwashi-no-Mikoto, {{ill|Futodama|lt=Ame-no-Futodama|Q11059539|qid=Q11059539|qid=Q11059539|lt=Ame-no-Futodama-no-Mikoto}}, Ame-no-Tomi-no-Mikoto, {{ill|Izanagi|Q813858|qid=Q813858|lt=Izanagi-no-Mikoto}}, and {{ill|Izanami|Q682306|qid=Q682306|lt=Izanami-no-Mikoto}} as principal deities. It also has associated deities including Aha-wakehiko-no-Mikoto and {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|Q272993|qid=Q272993|lt=Susanoo-no-Mikoto}}, and through merger of nearby shrines additionally enshrines the following 18 deities:

*{{ill|Sumiyoshi sanjin|lt=Sumiyoshi Ōkami|qid=Q1114013}}
*Takakurahiko-no-Mikoto
*Ōma-musubi-no-Mikoto
*Takarai-no-Mikoto and Kurarai-no-Mikoto
*{{ill|Takamimusubi|lt=Takamimusubi|UNKNOWN|qid=Q125400|lt=Takamimusubi-no-Kami}} and {{ill|Kamimusubi|lt=Kamimusubi|UNKNOWN|qid=Q3275901|lt=Kamimusubi-no-Kami}}
*{{ill|Yamato Takeru|Q461258|qid=Q461258|lt=Yamatotakeru-no-Mikoto}}
*{{ill|Kakinomoto no Hitomaro|Q380818|qid=Q380818|lt=Kakinomoto no Hitomaro}}
*{{ill|Kuraokami|Q644201|qid=Q644201|lt=Takamifuri-no-Mikoto and Shizumifuri-no-Mikoto}}
*{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Ame-no-Oshihi-no-Mikoto}}
*{{ill|Amaterasu|Q455602|qid=Q455602|lt=Amaterasu-Ōmikami}}
*Iso-ne-mikihime-no-Mikoto (wife of Ōmahikoko-no-Mikoto)
*{{ill|Princess Sotoorihime|Q11626419|qid=Q11626419|lt=Sotōrihime-no-Mikoto}}
*{{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|Q1781862|qid=Q1781862|lt=Konohanasakuya-hime-no-Mikoto}}
*{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kanayamahiko-no-Mikoto}}
*{{ill|Sugawara no Michizane|Q382005|qid=Q382005}}

''Gikeiki'' records that {{ill|Minamoto no Yoritomo|Q242800|qid=Q242800}}, after defeat at {{ill|Battle of Ishibashiyama|Q2888010|qid=Q2888010}}, fled to Awa; after worship at {{ill|Susaki Shrine|Q11556513|qid=Q11556513}}, he spent one night at Takiguchi Daimyōjin (this shrine). Before the Edo period it was called "Kotaka Myōjin" and "Takiguchi Myōjin."

A tradition says many deer lived in the area and troubled residents when Ame-no-Tomi-no-Mikoto and others landed in Awa, so deer hunting was performed. Based on this, a ritual hunt festival was held for ten days from old calendar November 26.

To the right of the haiden is Ten Shrine enshrining Amenominakanushi-no-Mikoto. It is a Shikinaisha that was merged into this shrine in 1928. The former Ten Shrine building was moved into these precincts and used as a mikoshi hall; later, after a new mikoshi hall was built, it was restored as the Ten Shrine building.

The Chikura shrine in Minamibōsō enshrines Ame-no-Hiwashi-no-Mikoto, Konohanasakuya-hime-no-Mikoto, and {{ill|Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto|lt=Tsukuyomi|Q595520|qid=Q595520|qid=Q595520|lt=Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto}}.

It is said that {{ill|Minamoto no Yoritomo|Q242800|qid=Q242800}}, who later opened the Kamakura shogunate, dedicated statues of Yoriyoshi and Yoshie and an image of Yakushi Nyorai to the branch Mitama Shirahata Shrine here, along with 600 volumes of the Great Prajñā Sutra copied by himself. The sutras were interred in a sutra mound in Meiwa 9 ({{ill|1772|Q7690|qid=Q7690}}).
